title: SPECIAL REPORT: Inside AI scam ads exploiting TikTok’s advertising system to defraud Nigerians

reading.body:
This is a case of impersonation carried out through synthetic media, and it happened inside a paid advertising system rather than in an organic post. The fraudsters used deepfake video and cloned voice to present themselves as banks, telecoms brands and named public figures, and they bought placement so the material was distributed as promotion. The harm landed on the people who responded to the offers, not on the brands being imitated.

The failure sits at the advertiser verification and content moderation stage of the ad pipeline. The ads ran as paid promotions, which means they passed through whatever review the platform applies before a campaign goes live, and the reporting says many carried no AI label and had comments disabled. Catching this would have required checking who was actually buying the ad space, detecting synthetic likeness of real people and brands, and moderating in the local languages the ads used. The reporting attributes the gap to weak advertiser checks and gaps in local-language moderation.

What is not established is the intent of any party beyond the fraudsters themselves, and the reporting does not say what happens next, so no enforcement action, takedown or legal outcome can be assumed. The figures for losses come from two individuals who described what they lost, and the count of archived ads is the reporter's own record over five weeks.

reports.title: SPECIAL REPORT: Inside AI scam ads exploiting TikTok’s advertising system to defraud Nigerians

summary:
A Premium Times investigation found that AI-generated scam ads are running as paid promotions on TikTok and defrauding Nigerians. Fraudsters use deepfake videos and cloned voices to impersonate brands such as OPay, UBA, MTN and Airtel, plus public figures including Aliko Dangote and Tony Elumelu. One teacher lost about N150,000 after a fake OPay ad promised a free PoS machine and a N200,000 grant, and a crypto trader lost holdings worth about N1 million. The reporter archived 130 such ads over five weeks, with OPay appearing in 28.

The ads promise grants, loans, giveaways and investment returns, and they link to foreign-registered websites that harvest personal details. Many had comments disabled and no AI labels. TikTok earns billions in ad revenue and reaches over 37 million Nigerians, yet its moderation failed to stop these promotions. Experts blame weak advertiser checks and gaps in local-language moderation. The article does not say what happens next.
